newsitem.title: ITALY: Pope, recovering from surgery, appeals for peace.
newsitem.headline: Pope, recovering from surgery, appeals for peace.

text.p: Pope John Paul, who is recovering from surgery, on Thursday urged humanity to leave behind the conflicts of the 20th century.
"Let us continue to pray to the God of peace so that women and men of our time learn to leave behind the horrible conflicts that have plagued history and our century in particular," he said.
The Papal message was read to religious leaders at the close of an international peace conference sponsored by the Sant' Egidio peace group, which has negotiated several international peace deals.
"I would have liked to be with you during this meeting ... I will be there spiritually," he wrote in the message read to the gathering by his secretary of state, Cardinal Angelo Sodano.
The Pope, recovering in hospital from surgery to remove his appendix, gathered religious leaders from around the world in the hilltown of Assisi in 1986 for a common prayer for peace.
"I am grateful to all participants who are keeping the spirit of Assisi alive," the Pope's message said.
During the 1986 meeting in the birthplace of St Francis, the Pope persuaded various warring parties around the world to stop fighting for at least 24 hours while he and others prayed for peace.
"During these 10 years many believers have learned to know each other better, to use the language of solidarity and to spread the message of peace in their areas," the Pope said.
